questions.q: If an attacker physically removes a server's drive, which parts of the CIA triad are affected?
options: Both confidentiality (data exposed) and availability (the system is now down)
Only integrity, since the data itself wasn't changed
Only availability, since confidentiality requires a network-based breach
None of the triad applies to physical theft
questions.explain: Stealing the drive exposes whatever data was on it and simultaneously takes down whatever system depended on it — two triad violations from one physical act.

questions.q: What is a mantrap designed to prevent?
options: Tailgating — an unauthorized person slipping in right behind someone with legitimate badge access
Overheating in a server room
Power outages affecting a data center
Fires from damaging electronic equipment
questions.explain: A mantrap's interlocking doors only let one verified person through at a time, which stops an unauthorized person from following someone in.

questions.q: Why do server rooms use specialized fire suppression agents instead of water sprinklers?
options: Because water would destroy the electronic equipment while putting out the fire
Because water is more expensive than other suppression agents
Because sprinklers are not legal in commercial buildings
Because fire suppression agents also function as a backup power source
questions.explain: Specialized agents fight the fire while minimizing damage to electronics, something a standard water sprinkler system would not do.

questions.q: What role does a UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply) play in a server room?
options: It bridges a power outage, keeping systems running until a graceful shutdown or generator takes over
It cools the server room during normal operation
It logs which employees badged into the building
It records video of the server room entrance
questions.explain: A UPS provides short-term battery backup power during an outage, covering the gap until shutdown procedures or backup generators take over.

questions.q: Why does physical security still matter for a company that runs everything in the cloud?
options: Because physical and environmental security hasn't gone away — responsibility for it has just shifted to the cloud provider
Because cloud companies are exempt from physical security requirements entirely
Because cloud-based data has no physical hardware behind it at all
Because physical security only applies to on-premises email servers
questions.explain: Cloud providers still run real data centers with badge access, cameras, and environmental controls — the company just isn't the one managing that layer directly.
